thought.text: Step 2 needs issuer/client/secret/audience. The guide's `nebu-admin` client is stale — the actual registered Dex client is `nebu-gateway`/`nebu-dev-secret`. Submitting step 2:

reasoning_content:
Step 2 requires oidc_issuer, oidc_client_id, oidc_client_secret, and oidc_audience. According to the compose file, the only registered Dex client is `nebu-gateway`, with secret `nebu-dev-secret`. Since the audience must match the client ID in JWT validation, the audience is `nebu-gateway`.

The guide says to use client `nebu-admin`/`nebu-admin-secret` — but that's outdated info (the compose file states that the nebu-admin client has been removed). Following the actual Dex configuration, use nebu-gateway/nebu-dev-secret.

Before submitting, verify that Dex is reachable from the server container (issuer http://dex:5556/dex — the server needs to be able to discover JWKS). Dex is healthy, and the server is on the same compose network, so the service name `dex` should resolve. Submit step 2.

action.command:
cd /tmp/nebu-bootstrap
CSRF=$(grep -o 'name="_csrf_token" value="[^"]*"' step2.html | sed 's/.*value="//;s/"//')
curl -s -b cookies.txt -c cookies.txt -e "http://localhost:8080/admin/bootstrap" --max-time 15 \
  --data-urlencode "_csrf_token=$CSRF" \
  --data-urlencode "oidc_issuer=http://dex:5556/dex" \
  --data-urlencode "oidc_client_id=nebu-gateway" \
  --data-urlencode "oidc_client_secret=nebu-dev-secret" \
  --data-urlencode "oidc_audience=nebu-gateway" \
  -o step2_resp.html -w "step2 POST: [%{http_code}]\n" http://localhost:8080/admin/bootstrap/step/2
grep -o 'Could not discover JWKS[^<]*' step2_resp.html | head -1
head -c 200 step2_resp.html; echo
